S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder is characterized by persistent preoccupation with perceived defects or flaws in appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others, accompanied by repetitive appearance-related behaviors or mental acts. It typically presents with avoidance, reassurance seeking, mirror checking, grooming, or comparison behaviors that become time-consuming and impair work, relationships, or daily functioning. It is distinguished from ordinary appearance dissatisfaction by its intensity, repetitiveness, and functional impact, and from eating-disorder body image concerns when the focus is not primarily weight or body fat.

patient.stressor_event: Changing to a different line of work
patient.stressor: As Mary Rucker began moving from long-familiar home-health aide work toward a supervisory role and CNA credential, she found herself newly exposed to staff meetings, credential photographs, video trainings, and closer scrutiny from families and administrators. What began as extra care before interviews and church or senior-center commitments gradually centered on a perceived facial and neck flaw that others either did not notice or described as minor, and she developed repeated checking, grooming, and mental comparison routines before leaving the house. Over an unclear period, the routines began making her late with documentation, avoid supervisory opportunities, and skip some book club and walking-club activities she had previously enjoyed. She eventually mentioned the problem during a primary-care visit for work paperwork, and her clinician referred her for psychiatric evaluation after recognizing the level of impairment.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I came in because I can’t stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck, and even when folks tell me it looks normal, I feel like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before I leave for work or a meeting, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror, fixing my collar and hair around my neck, taking another look in my phone camera, and sometimes asking my daughter if it looks strange, which has made me late more than once.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on the supervisory pieces because I worry people will be looking at my face and neck, and I’ve fallen behind on paperwork after getting stuck trying to make myself look presentable. I’ve also stopped going to some of my book club and walking club activities because getting ready feels like too much.
